scope: Fresh static disassembly of installed official Windows client and matching local AssetBundles. Ordinary native branches only; no game execution or runtime XLua override verification.

findings.claim: WeakDamage.TryGetWeakDamage reads current snapshot.atkInfo.atk and atkScale once, constructs PHYSICAL and MAGICAL candidate AttackInfo values using the same atk and atkScale, and calls CalculateDamageNoEvent twice.
WeakDamage.Execute compares the two values using RELATIVE_GT and changes the ongoing snapshot damageType. It does not apply either candidate to HP or replay calculation events.

AtkScaleUp.Execute merges or overwrites the same current snapshot.atkInfo.atkScale field used by weak comparison. Modifications performed before WeakDamage are visible to both candidates; modifications performed later are not retroactive.
The ordinary CalculateDamage entry calls source.OnCalculateDamage, then target.OnBeingCalculateDamage, then CalculateDamageNoEvent, then source.OnAfterCalculateDamage, subject to event flags.

Both common_weak_damage_buff and Mountain f12yin_t_atk_scale templates use event 14 (ON_CALCULATE_DAMAGE). The latter uses AtkScaleUp; the former uses WeakDamage after optional fixed-weakness handling. This does not establish a universal order between all critical mechanisms and weakness.

limits: Critical effects are not one universal action here. This evidence establishes how existing multiplier data is consumed, not that every critical effect executes before weakness.

The generic ProbAdditionNextAtkTalent.OnBeforeAttack native implementation performs a random gate and attaches an ability on success. The extracted Mountain component has a prob key, but its external MonoScript PPtr was not resolved; this generic class is not asserted to be that component solely from matching fields.

The native weak comparison uses the three-argument AttackInfo(atk,damageType,atkScale) constructor, which resets atkAddition to zero. PRTS lists atkAddition among weak comparison inputs. Runtime hotfix/version behavior for this difference has not been verified.
Metadata field offsets for value types in fields are boxed offsets; unboxed native AttackInfo and Snapshot accesses subtract the object-header size of 0x10.
